title: RBAC v2: Permission Replay & Fuzz Regression Suite
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a deterministic permission-replay and fuzzing regression harness for RBAC v2 that validates permission evaluation, audit-log fidelity, and SSO/SAML attribute mappings across service boundaries. This ticket delivers: 1) a replay engine that consumes recorded API request traces and corresponding audit log entries, 2) a directed-fuzz generator for permission combinations (roles, grants, resource attributes) to expand golden fixtures, and 3) CI integration that fails builds on policy regressions or audit log mismatches. Motivation: recent subtle regressions in permission inheritance and SAML attribute mapping caused two incidents. We need an automated, reproducible suite to catch regressions before customers are impacted.
implementation:
1) Define canonical event schema for replay (request context, principal, SAML attributes, resource, expected effect).
2) Extend existing golden fixtures format to include audit-log expectations (action, decision, reason, metadata).
3) Implement replay engine in Go: deterministic ordering, time-warp support, and pluggable policy-evaluator stubs for dedicated/private deployments.
4) Add a directed-fuzz generator: seed from production sampling, mutate role sets, allowlist/denylist combos, and generate fixtures labeled by risk score.
5) Create an aggregator that compares live policyEvaluator output against fixture expectations and emits structured failure diffs.
6) Wire into nightly CI and gating pipelines with configurable thresholds; automatically open ENG tickets for high-confidence regressions.
7) Document usage and onboarding steps for PM/Design/Eng reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Replay engine can ingest a fixture and deterministically reproduce the permission decision sequence
Generated fuzz fixtures increase coverage of policy surface by at least 45% (measured via policy decision coverage report)
CI job fails when a replay shows a decision mismatch or audit-log entry difference (action/decision/reason) for any golden fixture
Audit log replay validates attribute-level values for SAML mappings (email, groups, custom attributes) across at least 6 mapping patterns
Performance: replay of 5k fixtures completes under 30 minutes on standard CI runner (or scaled runner defined in pipeline)
Runbook added describing triage steps for regression failures and linking to policy evaluator logs and failing fixture artifact
test_plan:
- Unit tests for replay engine core primitives and fixture parser.
- Integration tests: run replay against a stubbed policy-evaluator with controlled responses.
- Golden regression: store a baseline of 500 fixtures; run nightly full-suite with differential output.
- Fuzz validation: equivocation check to ensure fuzz doesn't create impossible states.
- Load validation: run 10k small fixtures in CI canary cluster to measure runtime and memory.

notes: Trade-offs: full deterministic replay for all production traffic is expensive and may surface PII in fixtures; we will sanitize and sample. Fuzzing increases signal but may produce false positives; we will score and tier fixtures to prioritize human review. Long-term: integrate with runtime tracing to capture richer context. Short-term risk: test flakiness from non-deterministic side effects; mitigations included in implementation (time-warp, state snapshots).
